column1: # Bare generic instantiation used as a value (no call parens). These are the
# shapes that exposed the command-position NAME[...] fidelity divergence: the
# engine parses the subscript as ARITHMETIC, so a non-arithmetic one is a hard
# parse error where real bash 5.3 sees an ordinary glob word. Kept as a
# regression net for that defect, which is certification-owned, not Bash++'s.
# Recognized-but-UNSUPPORTED Go forms. Their class decides whether Bash++ may
# diagnose them or must fall back to shell: diagnosing a Class E form would
# break a working script, while diagnosing a Class R form costs nothing.
# COMMIT-POINT PREFIXES. A parser commits at the opening line, not after seeing
# the whole construct, so a multi-line construct must be classified at its
# PREFIX. These rows are the decision points, and they do not always agree with
# the complete form: `type T struct {` alone is an ordinary bash command (E)
# while the complete multi-line struct is a parse error (R). Classifying only
# the complete form would have recorded that site as free when it is not.
